# Keymap fixtures

Three compiled XKB keymaps, checked in so `crate::input::keymap`'s tests
assert against a **real** layout rather than against hand-written keysym
constants.

That distinction is the reason these files exist. The bug class WS-E.3.1
(issue #217, decision [D-028](../../../../docs/plan/20-decision-log.md)) is
built to prevent is *silent mistyping*: an evdev/xkb off-by-eight types `g`
where `ğ` was meant, and a legacy-vs-Unicode keysym mix-up drops `ğ ş ı İ`
while `ö ç ü` keep working. A test whose expected values were typed by the
same hand that wrote the code is wrong in exactly the same direction as the
code. These are not.

| File | Generated by | Bytes | What it is for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `keymap-us.xkb` | `xkbcli compile-keymap --layout us` | 71 249 | Shift levels, named keys, unbound scancodes |
| `keymap-tr.xkb` | `xkbcli compile-keymap --layout tr` | 73 028 | `ğ ş ı İ` — the legacy-keysym letters, and the `ğ`/`g` scancode pair |
| `keymap-us-lv3latch.xkb` | `xkbcli compile-keymap --layout us --options lv3:caps_switch_latch` | 71 319 | The resolve-before-update ordering, below |

Generated with `libxkbcommon` **1.13.2** against the system
`xkeyboard-config` data. To regenerate:

```sh
xkbcli compile-keymap --layout us > crates/vitrin-core/tests/fixtures/keymap-us.xkb
xkbcli compile-keymap --layout tr > crates/vitrin-core/tests/fixtures/keymap-tr.xkb
xkbcli compile-keymap --layout us --options lv3:caps_switch_latch \
  > crates/vitrin-core/tests/fixtures/keymap-us-lv3latch.xkb
```

## Why the third one is not exotic decoration

`lv3:caps_switch_latch` is a shipped `xkeyboard-config` option — Caps Lock
chooses the third level while held, and latches it — and it is the smallest
*real* keymap in which a modifier key's own event changes the level that key
resolves at. That makes the resolve-before-update ordering **observable**:

| | Caps press | Caps release |
|---|---|---|
| resolve, then update (correct) | `ISO_Level3_Shift` `0xfe03` | `ISO_Level3_Latch` `0xfe04` |
| update, then resolve (wrong) | `ISO_Level3_Latch` `0xfe04` | `ISO_Level3_Shift` `0xfe03` |

On `us` or `tr` the two orders agree on every sequence tried, which is
precisely why an ordering bug here is silent — and why the test needed a
keymap that can tell them apart. It is also, for free, a real keyboard on
which one key's press and release resolve to **different keysyms**, which is
the thing that broke keysym pairing in the first place.

Regenerating is not routine. A keymap that moved would move the tests'
expected keysyms, which is the assertion — so a diff here needs the same
reading a golden-frame diff gets.

## Why they are checked in and not compiled at test time

`crate::input::keymap` builds its `xkb::Context` with
`NO_DEFAULT_INCLUDES | NO_ENVIRONMENT_NAMES` on purpose: the core reaches no
XKB search path, so it *cannot* resolve `--layout tr` at run time even if a
test wanted it to. Checking the compiled output in is the only shape that
tests the production constructor. It also keeps the suite off the runner's
`xkeyboard-config` version, which would otherwise make a keysym assertion a
property of the CI image.
